issue.title: s(269) ≤ 16.899469075856: improved packing (registration request)
issue.body:
**Credit name.** Doğa Özden ([@dogaozden](https://github.com/dogaozden), https://dogaozden.com/math/live/square-packing/); improved_by Doğa Özden. The result was found by his AI research lab. This issue and the certificate repository were prepared and posted on his behalf by his AI agent, which uses the GitHub account `kenaznia-doga`.

**Claim.** `s(269) ≤ 16.899469075856` (the exact rational side of the witness, rounded up at 12 places). The record holds ` = 16.9009945799513249` (`packing/frontier/n-269.md`, T-290, our own packing (Doğa Özden, found_by; jlevy/squares#947), built from Nate Chaoweeraprasit's packing (itsnaka) improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd). **The improvement is 1.526e-03** (relative 9.03e-05). **This improves our own jlevy/squares#947, already registered as T-290 (16.9009945799513249), by 1.5255e-3; it is a further improvement of that registered record.** It is an upper bound only: no KKT, local-optimality, rigidity or global-optimality claim.

**Leaderboard, stated first.** Ours does NOT beat the Kaggle leaderboard's side-only entry for n = 269 (16.889730079125, elegans, 2026-11-05; cache of 2026-11-09, unpublished and unverifiable): ours is above it by 9.74e-3; it is 1.53e-3 below the registry record, our own #947 (T-290), and below the best public packing we know of. Details under "Other public values" below.

**Certificate.** A `Witness/v2` file (corners, rational scalars, 269 squares), `n-269-candidate.yaml`, in https://github.com/kenaznia-doga/s269-upper-bound-16899469076 at commit `fdab2c0073ea91701d0d8429663faa6e5c7f831f` (https://github.com/kenaznia-doga/s269-upper-bound-16899469076/tree/fdab2c0073ea91701d0d8429663faa6e5c7f831f). SHA-256 `54b408b2f1b45fc3d0a1330767c8740f0889eecb73f5fcf7888710526dbcc26b`. `n269-witness.json` is the same file as JSON. The exact coordinates were produced by this repository's own `packing-witness promote --strategy robust-rational` (@ 0af33d85) from our decimal pose: `center_dilation: '1'`, no dilation, so the pair margins of about 2e-13 are the decimal pose's own (left by the final f64 repair scaling of Evan Daniel's quench, about 1e-13 relative), rounded to 36 digits. The promotion puts the least corner coordinates at 0 and takes the side as the greatest, so only the squares that set the left wall, the bottom wall and the side touch them exactly; other squares near a wall clear it by up to about 1e-12. The decimal pose is in the repository as `n-269-decimal-pose.yaml`, which the witness's `source.path` names; `certificate.replay` names the repository's own file.

**Checking.**
- This repository's `packing-witness verify` (jlevy/squares `main` @ 0af33d85, run unmodified on the file placed under `packing/witnesses/known-best/`): `VERIFIED`, method exact-algebraic, 36046 pairs tested. Output in `packing-witness-verify.txt`.
- `sqcheck.py` (in the repo), our own exact checker written separately from the registry's code: `VALID`, exact rational. Output in `sqcheck-output.txt`.
- Before promotion, `sqcheck.py` also certified the decimal pose in interval arithmetic at its own side.
- The exact side minus the record's exact side is negative in `Fraction` arithmetic.
- Rerun commands are in the README.

**What the checkers share.** The unit-square, wall and non-overlap definitions only. The promotion to rationals used your tool, so `packing-witness verify` is not independent of how the coordinates were rounded; `sqcheck.py` is.

**Not done.** No local-optimality or rigidity analysis. No formal proof-assistant check. No human review outside our project. We found no open jlevy/squares issue or PR for n = 269 below the record (checked 0af33d85, 2026-11-11 15:35 PST), and nothing better for it in evand/square-packing @ c801ab47.

**Lineage and credit.** The record's holders as the registry lists them: Doğa Özden (found_by; our issue #947), a packing found by transplanting Evan Daniel's n = 304 packing. Found by an AI-run band-design search, new for this filing (tilted squares from a registry packing of the same family laid along the diagonal as a seed band; simulated annealing in a reduced model in which the tilted squares move freely and the axis-parallel squares sit on the two wall-anchored staircase lattices, present or absent, with the overlap of the squares that must be kept as energy; then one quench with Evan Daniel's ALM+SLP code). This packing was built from tilted squares of three clusters of registry or own packings: the second cluster of tilted squares of the registry's n = 207 packing (`207b`), the cluster of the registry's n = 70 packing (`70a`; Ryan Xu, found_by; improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd), and the first cluster of our own n = 179 band packing (`179ha`, jlevy/squares#954), each reflected in the main diagonal of its box (symmetry 2; shifts (0, 0), (0, 0) and (3, 3), our band tool's `[207b, 2, 0, 0, 0]`, `[70a, 2, 0, 0, 0]`, `[179ha, 2, 3, 3, 0]`) and rotated to a lean of 2.55°, 45 tilted squares at band parameter 0.899, annealed at that side (2e7 moves, energy 0.0719) and quenched once to 16.899469084224 (job b1n269r2, trial at 4806 s). A random kick of that packing's coordinates (sigma 0.0031) and a second quench, 18 s later in the same job, gave 16.899469075879, and a further kick (sigma 0.0296) and quench, 3 s after that, gave the filed side 16.899469075855. The filed packing has 46 tilted squares (the record, our #947, has 100); 16 of them share the angle -42.88° (it is not one clean band). Squares matched by assignment up to the symmetries of the square: 262 of 269 centres move by more than 1e-3, 124 by more than 0.05 (largest 1.456); 116 squares are re-tilted by more than 1° (largest 44.77°); the packing has 46 squares tilted by more than 0.5° against the record's 100. See `records/n-269-candidate-diff.png`. Credit the improvement to Doğa Özden, the band's source packing to n = 207 (registry), n = 70 (Ryan Xu; improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd) and our own n = 179 (#954) and the current record to its holders as the registry lists them, and the local optimizer to Evan Daniel (`search/packer`, MIT, @ bb4cc78e).

**Licence.** The repository carries `LICENSE.md`: CC BY 4.0 for the witness, data and text; MIT for code. It also carries Evan Daniel's MIT notice, `LICENSE-evand-square-packing.txt`.

**Other public values, for context.** The best public Kaggle per-puzzle packing we found for 269 has side 16.901513582205 (kirilltym; dataset refreshed 2026-11-11 03:32Z), above ours. The Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard (staff notebook inversion/squares-in-squares-per-puzzle-leaderboard; cache of 2026-11-09 20:52Z) lists a side-only entry for n = 269: **16.889730079125**, team elegans, 2026-11-05. It is unpublished and states no packing, so we cannot verify it and make no claim about it. **Ours does not beat it: it is above it by 9.74e-3** (our exact side 16.8994690758550465, claim 16.899469075856). The cache is from 2026-11-09 20:52Z. Ours is 1.53e-3 below the registry record (our own #947, T-290) and below the best public packing we know of (16.901513582205, kirilltym), so it is the best published packing with a certificate we know of, not the smallest side anyone has scored.

**AI assistance.** Yes, throughout. The search and its code were written and run by AI agents; the checks above were run by code that did not produce the packing. Doğa directed the work and asked that our results be registered.

It does not beat the Kaggle leaderboard's side-only entry for n = 269 (16.889730079125, cache of 2026-11-09): it is above it by 9.74e-3.
